To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sign of the causal treatment effect is identifiable in the competing risks model if the copula is independent of the covariate and can be estimated by the sign of the change in the subdistribution.
the sign of a covariate effect is identifiable in the competing risks model if the copula is independent of the covariate.
the sign of the causal treatment effect is identifiable if the copula is independent of the covariate and that the sign of this effect is invariant with respect to changes in the copula.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the causal effects in the competing risks model.
a new approach to identify the effect of a treatment in the competing risks model.
the identifiability and estimation of the sign of a causal covariate effect in the competing risks model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sign of the effect of a covariate is identifiable in the competing risks model if the copula is independent of the covariate.
our method is a valuable supplement to existing methods for the analysis of competing risks data.
the sign of the effect of the treatment on the duration time is identifiable if the copula of the competing risks is independent of the treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sign of the marginal covariate effect is identifiable even if the copulas are mainly unspecified.
the sign of the marginal treatment effect is identifiable and can be consistently estimated in the competing risks model even if the copular function is mainly unspecified.
the competing risks approach to duration analysis is a very powerful tool for empirical research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is often possible to obtain informative estimates of the sign of the causal effect in competing risks settings even when the copula is mainly unspecified or not of interest.
the sign of the causal treatment effect can be identified in a large class of competing risks models.
the sign of the marginal effect of a covariate is identifiable in the competing risks model if the dependence structure is not a function of the varying covariates.
